title: Cyclic Fueter Theory: Lean 4 Formalization of Selected Results
description:
This software repository contains Lean 4 source files developed in connection with the Cyclic Fueter Theory (CFT) research program. It formalizes selected algebraic and geometric statements involving quaternionic algebra, Fueter-type operators, matrix and spinor constructions, quantum-geometric identities, Cartan-frame calculations, the reduced Einstein–Yang–Mills action and its four-dimensional field equations, distributional junction conditions, characteristic evolution and constraint propagation, zero-mode calculations, and consequences of the action principle for the Einstein–Yang–Mills dumbbell (caps as closed radiation universes, the AdS₂ × S² neck, JT/Schwarzian reduction, thermodynamics, and stability).

Version 0.4.0 contains 1544 theorem declarations in 141 modules, with no sorry and no project-specific axioms, plus 244 index aliases. New in this version: the claim ledger is restructured as kinematics (which part and quantity of the dumbbell) → action → dynamics, with an index module; an independent sceptical audit and its corrections (magnetic Euclidean action of the neck, the JT dilaton in neck coordinates, the true quadratic form of the neck instability with a growth-rate bound, the ellipsoidal S⁹ at first order, and a negative result on internal zero modes); an adjoint Higgs field that keeps the neck exact and makes it stable for every length when m_W²ℓ² ≥ 3/4; and replacements of citations and weak checks by the dumbbell's own geometry (spherically symmetric global classification, four-dimensional Einstein equations on the neck, the cap's maximal radius equal to the neck radius, Tolman–Ehrenfest on the neck, geodesic deviation on the Euclidean neck, the exact Schwarzian density of states, conservation of the quantum back-reaction on the cap, and an attractor form of the higher-derivative extremality condition). The repository includes an author-maintained status ledger of 107 items in α-I–α-XI (50 complete, 35 complete using a named external theorem, 9 complete in a differential field pending a bridge to real functions, 5 partial, 8 not started). These labels describe the current scope of this formalization; they are not independent certification or peer review of the corresponding research claims. Lean verifies each theorem from its declared assumptions and imported results. Formalization does not by itself establish that a physical model, external theorem, or interpretation is appropriate.

The project targets Lean 4.15.0 and Mathlib v4.15.0. To reproduce the build, install Elan and run `lake update`, `lake exe cache get`, and `lake build` from the repository root.
